tools.name: brp_extras_screenshot
tools.title: take screenshot
tools.description:
Capture the primary window, a camera viewport, or an entity crop in one call.

Examples:
- Full window: {"path":"/tmp/full.png","port":15702}
- Camera viewport: {"camera":4294967297,"path":"/tmp/camera.png","port":15702}
- Entity ID: {"entity":4294967298,"path":"/tmp/entity.png","port":15702}
- Entity name: {"name":"NatesList","path":"/tmp/nates-list.png","port":15702}

Parameters:
- path: Required PNG destination.
- entity: Optional canonical u64 Bevy entity ID.
- name: Optional one-call lookup of a unique, case-sensitive exact Bevy Name.
- camera: Optional camera entity ID. Alone, captures its viewport; with entity or name, selects the
  camera used for the crop.
- padding: Optional physical-pixel padding around an entity crop; defaults to zero.
- port: BRP port; defaults to 15702.

Use either entity or name, never both. Padding requires one of them. A name capture internally uses
the same standard world.query lookup as world_find_entities_by_name, requires one exact match, and
sends only the resolved entity ID to bevy_brp_extras. Use world_find_entities_by_name first when you
want non-exact discovery, need to inspect duplicate matches, or want to choose the entity ID yourself.

Entity crops require the entity to be visible to the selected camera. If camera is omitted, exactly
one eligible camera must be unambiguous. Crops use AABB bounds, or Bevy UI bounds when the
bevy_brp_extras ui feature is enabled. They contain the final composited pixels inside the bounds,
not an isolated render of the entity.

The call returns only after the PNG is completely encoded and atomically published; filesystem
polling is unnecessary. A minimized, hidden, or fully occluded primary window may legitimately
produce a black image on platforms that stop presenting it.

Requires bevy_brp_extras and BrpExtrasPlugin in the target application.

entity.description: Canonical Bevy entity ID to capture.

name.description: Unique, case-sensitive exact Bevy `Name` to resolve before capture.

camera.description: Camera entity ID. Captures its viewport, or selects it for an entity crop.

padding.description: Physical pixels to add around an entity crop. Defaults to zero.

path.description: File path where the complete PNG should be published.

port.description: Port number for BRP - defaults to 15702

tools.name: brp_extras_type_text
tools.title: type text sequentially
tools.description:
Types text sequentially in Bevy apps via bevy_brp_extras. Characters are typed one per frame with proper key press/release cycles, simulating realistic human typing.

Unlike `send_keys` which sends all keys simultaneously (for chords and shortcuts), `type_text` queues characters and types them sequentially. This is ideal for text input fields that need to process each character individually.

Supported characters:
- Letters (a-z, A-Z) - uppercase uses Shift
- Digits (0-9)
- Common symbols (!@#$%^&*()-=_+[]{}|;':",.<>/?\`~)
- Whitespace (space, newline, tab)

Characters that cannot be mapped will be skipped and reported in the response.

Examples:
```json
{"text": "hello world"}           // Types 11 characters across 11 frames
{"text": "Hello, World!\n"}       // Mixed case with punctuation and newline
{"text": "test@example.com"}      // Email address with @ symbol
```

Prerequisites: bevy_brp_extras dependency and BrpExtrasPlugin registered.

text.description: Text to type (supports letters, numbers, symbols, newlines, tabs)

tools.name: brp_launch
tools.title: launch bevy app or example
tools.description:
Launches Bevy apps or examples using unified target search.

Searches for the target by name across both apps and examples. Use search_order to control priority:
- "app" (default): searches apps first, then examples
- "example": searches examples first, then apps

The response includes a launched_as field ("app" or "example") indicating how the target was resolved.

If the target is not found as either type, returns an enriched error with an available_targets array listing all apps and examples (name, kind, path). Present these to the user as a table so they can pick the correct target.

Optional args parameter passes command-line arguments to the launched process. For apps, args are appended directly. For examples, args are passed after a `--` separator (cargo run --example foo -- args...).

Features: Non-blocking execution, temp directory logs, debug/release profiles, multi-instance support.

Multi-instance launching:
- When instance_count > 1, launches multiple instances on sequential ports starting from the specified port.
- Each instance gets its own log file with port in filename

Notes:
- App launches use a lock-free freshness check before invoking Cargo. If the binary appears up to date, the tool launches it directly without running cargo build. If the binary is missing, stale, or freshness cannot be determined confidently, the tool runs cargo build first.
- Example launches always invoke cargo run --example. Cargo decides whether the example is already fresh or needs rebuilding.
- Optional `path` parameter overrides the default search roots (MCP workspace roots / cwd). When provided, only the specified OS-level directory is searched for Bevy projects.
- If multiple targets with the same name exist in different packages, you must specify the package_name parameter.
- `package_name` matches the `package_name` field returned by `brp_list_bevy` for exact disambiguation.
- When specifying a port, bevy_brp_extras is required to support listening on the environment variable BRP_EXTRAS_PORT.

annotations.title: App: launch bevy app or example

target_name.description: Name of the Bevy target to launch (app or example)

profile.description: Build profile to use (debug or release)

path.description:
Optional OS-level path to use as the search root. Overrides the default MCP workspace
roots.

package_name.description: Package name to filter when multiple targets with the same name exist

port.description: Port number for BRP - defaults to 15702

instance_count.description:
Count of instances to launch in sequence
Validates count is within 1-100 - defaults to 1

env.description: Optional environment variables to set on the launched process

search_order.description:
Search order for target resolution: "app" searches apps first (default), "example" searches
examples first

args.description: Optional command-line arguments to pass to the launched process

tools.description:
List curated BRP records published by the running application's developer.

The public structured result puts instructions in result.usage and records in result.tools. Each

usage, then pass a selected method and matching raw params to brp_execute. Records are not native
MCP tools; rpc_discover instead exhaustively lists transport method names.

Each request validates every record against the live instant methods and returns either the full
list or an error if any method is missing or watching. A missing endpoint means the app needs
BrpExtrasPlugin; an installed endpoint may return an empty list. Direct HTTP JSON-RPC is a
developer-only alternative.

tools.name: brp_list_bevy
tools.title: list bevy apps and examples
tools.description:
Discovers all Bevy apps and examples declared in workspace Cargo.toml files via cargo metadata.
Targets not registered in Cargo.toml are not included.
Returns target names, kind (app or example), BRP support level, build profiles, build status, and paths.
Each item includes a `kind` field ("app" or "example") and `brp_level` field:
  - "extras": Uses `BrpExtrasPlugin` (full support: screenshots, input simulation, clean shutdown, etc.)
  - "brp_only": Uses `RemotePlugin` only (core BRP queries and mutations, no extras methods)
  - "none": No BRP support detected
For bins, `brp_level` reflects whether the package's src/ tree uses BRP plugins.
For examples, the individual source file is checked for BRP plugin imports.
Optional `path` parameter overrides the default search roots (MCP workspace roots / cwd). When provided, only the specified OS-level directory is searched for Bevy projects.
Use `package_name` with `brp_launch`'s `package_name` parameter to disambiguate targets with the same name.

tools.name: world_find_entities_by_name
tools.title: find entities by name
tools.description:
Discover canonical entity IDs by matching reflected Bevy Name components through standard BRP.

This MCP-local composite calls world.query directly. It requires RemotePlugin and a reflected
bevy_ecs::name::Name component.

Parameters:
- name: Case-sensitive text to match.
- match_mode: exact (default), prefix, suffix, or contains.
- port: BRP port, default 15702.

Match modes are explicit. Asterisks are ordinary characters and never act as wildcards.

The result contains entries with:
- entity: canonical u64 entity ID.
- name: complete reflected Name value.

Entries are sorted by entity ID. Duplicate names return every matching entity. No matches return an
empty list.

Examples:
- Exact: {"name":"NatesList"}
- Prefix: {"name":"Nates","match_mode":"prefix"}
- Suffix: {"name":"List","match_mode":"suffix"}
- Contains: {"name":"tesL","match_mode":"contains"}

brp_extras_screenshot accepts a unique exact name directly and uses this same lookup internally.
Call this tool yourself for non-exact discovery, duplicate matches, or explicit selection, then pass
the returned canonical entity ID to screenshot, mutation, inspection, or watch operations. Entity
IDs are the unambiguous identifier when names are duplicated.

name.description: Case-sensitive text to compare with reflected Bevy `Name` components.

match_mode.description: How an entity's case-sensitive [`Name`] must match the requested text.

port.description: Port number for BRP - defaults to 15702

tools.description:
Mutates component fields via `world.mutate_components` BRP method. Updates specific fields without replacing entire component.

Path syntax:
- Root replacement: "" (empty string to replace entire component)
- Nested: ".transform.translation.x"
- Arrays: ".points[2]"
- Tuples: ".0", ".1"
- Leading dot required for field paths

Example:
```json
{
  "entity": 123,
  "component": "bevy_transform::components::transform::Transform",
  "path": ".translation.y",
  "value": 10.5
}
```

Benefits: Preserves other fields, efficient for updates, ideal for animation.

Errors: Entity/component not found, invalid path, type mismatch.
Note: Requires BRP registration and reflection.

tools.name: world_trigger_event
tools.title: trigger event
tools.description:
Triggers an event in the Bevy world. This allows remote triggering of game events like spawning enemies, changing game state, or triggering cutscenes.

## Requirements

Events must be registered with reflection to be triggerable:

```rust
#[derive(Event, Reflect)]
#[reflect(Event)]
pub struct SpawnEnemy {
    pub enemy_type: String,
    pub position: Vec3,
}

// In your app setup:
app.register_type::<SpawnEnemy>();
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `event` | string | Yes | Full type path of the event (e.g., "my_game::SpawnEnemy") |
| `value` | object | No | Event payload as JSON. Omit for unit events (events with no data). |
| `port` | number | No | BRP port (default: 15702) |

## Examples

### Unit Event (no payload)

Trigger a simple event with no data:

```json
{
  "event": "my_game::events::PauseGame"
}
```

### Event with Payload

Trigger an event with structured data:

```json
{
  "event": "my_game::events::SpawnEnemy",
  "value": {
    "enemy_type": "goblin",
    "position": [10.0, 0.0, 5.0]
  }
}
```

### Event with Entity Reference

Events can reference entities:

```json
{
  "event": "my_game::events::DamageEntity",
  "value": {
    "target": 4294967299,
    "amount": 50
  }
}
```

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause |
|-------|-------|
| "Unknown event type" | Event type not registered in the type registry |
| "Event is not reflectable" | Event missing `#[reflect(Event)]` attribute |
| "is invalid" | Payload doesn't match expected event structure |

## Notes

- Events are triggered globally via `World::trigger()`, not targeted at specific entities
- The event must have `#[reflect(Event)]` to be discoverable and triggerable
- Use `brp_type_guide` or `registry_schema` to discover available event types

event.description: The full type path of the event to trigger (e.g., "`my_game::events::SpawnEnemy`")

value.description: The event payload as JSON. Omit for unit events (events with no data).

port.description: Port number for BRP - defaults to 15702

BRP tool execution (calls Bevy Remote Protocol)
